summary: The fix is real and I could not refute it. I reproduced both failure states myself rather than trusting the logs. Against the pre-fix files the screen test scores 2 pass / 5 fail; against the pre-236 view the database test scores 3 pass / 4 fail. After the change both are 7/7. Migration 236 applies cleanly onto a database that has never seen it, and it appends the new column last, so the view swap is legal. No money column, no new outbound call, no secret, no journey file touched, no route needed, no test weakened or skipped, no drive-by edit of anything outside the unit. HTML tags balance and every file grew rather than shrank. One real problem stops this from being clean: the branch's test suite is now red. A shared test file keeps a list of screens known to load their data too early, brand-studio.html is still on that list, and the test goes red on purpose when a listed screen gets fixed. The unit disclosed this honestly and left the file alone because another thread owns it, but the one-line deletion has to land in the same commit or the suite ships red. That same list labels brand-studio.html as belonging to thread T11, not T10, so two threads may believe they own this screen — worth settling before merge. Smaller notes: the write-up says the address box "fed the disclosure template", and nothing in the code actually injects it anywhere today; that is documented intent from migration 043, not shipped behaviour. And no browser walk was run on a screen-timing fix, which is exactly the class of bug a browser proves best.

violations.what: The branch test suite is red as a direct result of this unit's change. src/http/calendar-paint.test.mjs test 9 ('the known-unfixed list is still true') now fails: brand-studio.html is fixed but its line remains in KNOWN_UNFIXED. The unit disclosed this and did not touch the file because another thread owns it, but the fix is not shippable until that one-line deletion lands in the same commit.
violations.evidence: cd /tmp/wt-T10 && node --test src/http/calendar-paint.test.mjs -> '# pass 8 / # fail 1', 'not ok 9 - the known-unfixed list is still true'. KNOWN_UNFIXED still holds the entry at line 85.

violations.what: KNOWN_UNFIXED attributes brand-studio.html to thread T11, not T10. This unit edited a screen another thread's own test file records as T11's. If T11 is editing the same file in parallel, the merge collides on the exact block that was rewritten.
violations.evidence: "brand-studio.html": "T11 — line ~1282 `if (typeof FHData === \"undefined\" || !FHData.orgBrand) return;` runs during page parse, so the saved brand is never read back." — the same file the unit's boardRequest asks another thread to edit.

violations.what: The manifest says the address box "was the only box that fed the disclosure template", present tense. Nothing in the codebase injects entity_address into any template. Its only consumers are the endpoint's writable list, its length cap, the screen, and the two new tests. The claim comes from migration 043's stated intent, not from any shipped code path.
violations.evidence: grep -rn 'entity_address' api src db public netlify scripts -> only api/partner-brand.mjs (WRITABLE, TEXT_MAX, comments), the two new tests, and migration 236. No template, no disclosure renderer, no mail path references it.

violations.what: No browser run on a fix whose entire subject is script timing in a browser. The two new tests are a source-shape check and a database round-trip; neither loads the page. Disclosed by the unit as left undone, but it means nobody has watched the Brand Studio boxes fill in.
violations.evidence: manifest leftUndone: 'No Playwright walk was run'. The T10 walk screenshots under docs/workflows/ui-audit-evidence/T10-walk-brand-studio/ are dated 2026-08-18 23:58, before this unit's edits.

violations.what: An address cleared on the server will still appear in the box after a reload. load() merges a localStorage draft over the defaults, and the new mapping only overwrites when the server value is truthy, so a NULL from the server leaves the stale local value on screen. This matches every other field on the screen (entity, email, domain all use the same 'if truthy' guard), so it is the file's existing convention rather than something this unit introduced — but it is the one case where the round-trip claim does not hold.
violations.evidence: line 583 load(): 'var v = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)||"null"); if(v) Object.assign(D, v);' combined with line 1176 'if (b.entity_address) D.addr = b.entity_address;'

violations.check: 8 — journeys, branch level not unit level
violations.what: npm run journeys:check reports 9 stale files on this branch. Not attributable to this unit: the generator reads netlify/functions/api.mjs and api/ handlers, this unit added no route and only comments to api/partner-brand.mjs, and the stale set matches the routes sibling units added. Flagging so the orchestrator runs npm run journeys before committing.
violations.evidence: npm run journeys:check -> 'docs/journeys is stale — 9 file(s) out of date'. git status --porcelain docs/journeys is empty, so no -intended.md was touched.

violations.what: v_partner_brand_effective is not declared security_invoker and is owned by a superuser, so it does not enforce row-level security. Migration 236 adds a new column of partner data to that view. This is unchanged from 043 and partners/partner_brand both have RLS disabled anyway, so it is not a regression — but the only thing keeping one partner out of another's address is canAccessBrand in the handler.
violations.evidence: pg_class for v_partner_brand_effective: relowner=zootimusmaximus, reloptions NULL. relrowsecurity is false on both partners and partner_brand. The new pg test does prove the handler gate: 'a partner reaches their OWN brand and no other partner's' returns 403 for a rival.
